meta.title: Teaching Approaches & Lesson Frameworks
meta.randomizationRule: Randomize question selection/order and answer-option order on every attempt; never reuse an exact attempt signature.
meta.alignment: TKT Module 1 — Background to language teaching: teaching approaches, frameworks and procedures

questions.prompt: The teacher presents a new structure in context, gives controlled practice, then moves to freer use. Which framework is this?
questions.correctAnswer: Presentation, Practice and Production (PPP)
questions.explanation: PPP typically moves from presentation to controlled practice and then toward freer production.

questions.prompt: Which stage comes first in a typical PPP sequence?
questions.correctAnswer: Presentation
questions.explanation: PPP begins by introducing and clarifying the target language.

questions.prompt: Which activity best fits the Practice stage of PPP?
options: Complete controlled sentences using the target structure
Debate any topic using any language
Do a diagnostic task before teaching
questions.correctAnswer: Complete controlled sentences using the target structure
questions.explanation: The Practice stage normally gives guided or controlled use of the target language.

questions.prompt: Which activity best fits the Production stage of PPP?
options: Use the target language in a freer role-play
questions.correctAnswer: Use the target language in a freer role-play
questions.explanation: Production gives learners greater freedom to use the target language communicatively.

questions.prompt: Which statement about PPP is most accurate?
options: It usually moves from teacher-supported presentation toward increasingly independent use
It always begins with a free task before teaching
It avoids explicit focus on language
questions.correctAnswer: It usually moves from teacher-supported presentation toward increasingly independent use
questions.explanation: PPP typically sequences presentation, guided practice and freer production.

questions.prompt: A lesson follows: context → explanation of target language → gap-fill practice → freer speaking. Which framework is this?
questions.correctAnswer: PPP
questions.explanation: The sequence matches Presentation, Practice and Production.

questions.prompt: Which learner preference is often compatible with PPP?
options: Learners who like a clear focus on new language before freer use
Learners who want only open tasks with no prior language focus
Learners who want grammar rules followed by translation only
questions.correctAnswer: Learners who like a clear focus on new language before freer use
questions.explanation: PPP provides an explicit focus on language followed by supported practice.

questions.prompt: What mainly distinguishes PPP from Test-teach-test?
options: PPP normally teaches before testing freer use; Test-teach-test begins with a diagnostic task
questions.correctAnswer: PPP normally teaches before testing freer use; Test-teach-test begins with a diagnostic task
questions.explanation: Test-teach-test starts by seeing what learners can already do, whereas PPP usually presents first.

questions.prompt: Which sequence is most typical of PPP?
questions.correctAnswer: Present → controlled practice → freer practice
questions.explanation: This is the defining sequence of PPP.

questions.prompt: Which criticism is sometimes made of a rigid PPP lesson?
options: Learners may have limited opportunity to discover needs before the target language is selected
questions.correctAnswer: Learners may have limited opportunity to discover needs before the target language is selected
questions.explanation: A rigid PPP sequence can be less responsive to learner-generated language needs than diagnostic or task-first frameworks.

questions.prompt: Learners first complete a meaningful task, then discuss the language they used. Which approach is this?
questions.correctAnswer: Task-based learning (TBL)
questions.explanation: TBL organises learning around completion of meaningful tasks, followed by language focus.

questions.prompt: What is central in Task-based Learning?
questions.correctAnswer: Completing a meaningful task
questions.explanation: The task is the central organising feature of TBL.

questions.prompt: Which activity best fits TBL?
options: Plan a class trip together, then review useful language that emerged
Study a rule, then translate a paragraph
questions.correctAnswer: Plan a class trip together, then review useful language that emerged
questions.explanation: The lesson begins with meaning-focused task completion and later examines language.

questions.prompt: Why is language focus often placed after a task in TBL?
options: Learners' actual language use can reveal useful forms to notice or improve
Grammar should never be discussed before a task
The task has no learning purpose
questions.correctAnswer: Learners' actual language use can reveal useful forms to notice or improve
questions.explanation: Task performance can create a meaningful basis for subsequent language analysis.

questions.prompt: Which statement about TBL is most accurate?
options: Meaningful task completion is central, and language analysis can follow the task
The main aim is sentence translation
The teacher must present all target language before any task
questions.correctAnswer: Meaningful task completion is central, and language analysis can follow the task
questions.explanation: TBL typically prioritises task completion before focusing more explicitly on language.

questions.prompt: A lesson begins with learners solving a real-world problem in groups, followed by discussion of useful language. Which framework is this?
questions.correctAnswer: TBL
questions.explanation: The task comes first and language focus follows.

questions.prompt: Which learner preference may suit TBL?
options: Learners who like communicating to achieve an outcome
Learners who want grammar rules followed only by translation
Learners who prefer only repetition drills
questions.correctAnswer: Learners who like communicating to achieve an outcome
questions.explanation: TBL gives learners a reason to use language to complete meaningful tasks.

questions.prompt: What distinguishes TBL from PPP most clearly?
options: TBL typically starts from a task; PPP typically starts from presentation of target language
questions.correctAnswer: TBL typically starts from a task; PPP typically starts from presentation of target language
questions.explanation: The sequencing and central role of the task distinguish the two frameworks.

questions.prompt: Which sequence best matches TBL?
questions.correctAnswer: Task → discussion/language focus
questions.explanation: Cambridge's TKT worksheet links TBL with task completion followed by focus on language used in the task.

questions.prompt: Why can TBL help reveal learner needs?
options: The task can show what learners can and cannot yet express successfully
The task removes the need for feedback
questions.correctAnswer: The task can show what learners can and cannot yet express successfully
questions.explanation: Real task performance can expose gaps in learners' available language.

questions.prompt: Learners first try a task, the teacher teaches what they need, then they try another task. Which framework is this?
questions.correctAnswer: Test-teach-test
questions.explanation: Test-teach-test begins by diagnosing learner performance, then teaches relevant language, then checks improvement.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the first 'test' in Test-teach-test?
options: Find out what learners can already do
questions.correctAnswer: Find out what learners can already do
questions.explanation: The first task diagnoses strengths, gaps and prior knowledge.

questions.prompt: Why can Test-teach-test be efficient with stronger learners?
options: The teacher can avoid spending too long teaching language learners already know
questions.correctAnswer: The teacher can avoid spending too long teaching language learners already know
questions.explanation: The initial task helps target teaching more precisely.

questions.prompt: Which sequence best represents Test-teach-test?
options: Diagnostic task → targeted teaching → second task
questions.correctAnswer: Diagnostic task → targeted teaching → second task
questions.explanation: The first task identifies needs, the teaching addresses them, and the second task checks progress.

questions.prompt: What is a key advantage of Test-teach-test?
options: Teaching can respond directly to learner performance
It guarantees all learners need the same language
questions.correctAnswer: Teaching can respond directly to learner performance
questions.explanation: The diagnostic first stage provides evidence for what should be taught.

questions.prompt: Learners attempt a conditional-sentence task before any explanation. The teacher then clarifies problem areas and gives a second task. Which framework is this?
questions.correctAnswer: Test-teach-test
questions.explanation: The sequence is diagnostic attempt, teaching, then re-attempt.

questions.prompt: Which learner group may particularly benefit from Test-teach-test?
options: Learners who may already know some of the target language
Learners who must always begin with full teacher presentation
questions.correctAnswer: Learners who may already know some of the target language
questions.explanation: The framework identifies what learners already control and what still needs teaching.

questions.prompt: What distinguishes the first stage of Test-teach-test from the first stage of PPP?
options: It diagnoses existing ability before explicit teaching
questions.correctAnswer: It diagnoses existing ability before explicit teaching
questions.explanation: Test-teach-test starts with learner performance rather than teacher presentation.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the final 'test'?
options: Check whether learners can use the language more successfully after teaching
questions.correctAnswer: Check whether learners can use the language more successfully after teaching
questions.explanation: The second task provides evidence of learning after targeted teaching.

questions.prompt: Which statement about Test-teach-test is most accurate?
options: It is diagnostic and responsive to learner needs
It requires the teacher to pre-teach everything
questions.correctAnswer: It is diagnostic and responsive to learner needs
questions.explanation: Its first stage helps determine what teaching is actually necessary.

questions.prompt: Learners study examples and work out the grammar rule themselves. Which approach is this?
questions.correctAnswer: Guided discovery
questions.explanation: Guided discovery gives learners examples and support so they can infer rules or patterns.

questions.prompt: What is the teacher's role in guided discovery?
options: Provide examples and questions that help learners discover the rule
Give the rule immediately every time
questions.correctAnswer: Provide examples and questions that help learners discover the rule
questions.explanation: The teacher guides learners toward noticing and formulating the rule.

questions.prompt: Which activity best fits guided discovery?
options: Compare examples and answer questions about how a tense is formed and used
Translate a paragraph after reading a rule
questions.correctAnswer: Compare examples and answer questions about how a tense is formed and used
questions.explanation: Learners use examples and guiding questions to infer the pattern.

questions.prompt: Why can guided discovery promote learner involvement?
options: Learners actively analyse examples rather than only receiving a rule
questions.correctAnswer: Learners actively analyse examples rather than only receiving a rule
questions.explanation: The approach encourages cognitive engagement with language patterns.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes guided discovery?
options: The teacher structures the discovery process but learners work out key rules or patterns
Learners receive no examples or help
The lesson must contain no explicit discussion of form
questions.correctAnswer: The teacher structures the discovery process but learners work out key rules or patterns
questions.explanation: It is guided—not unsupported—discovery.

questions.prompt: Learners underline several examples of comparatives, answer questions, then formulate the rule. What approach is this?
questions.correctAnswer: Guided discovery
questions.explanation: Learners infer the rule from examples with teacher guidance.

questions.prompt: Which sequence best represents guided discovery?
options: Examples → learners work out rule → practice
questions.correctAnswer: Examples → learners work out rule → practice
questions.explanation: This sequence appears directly in Cambridge's TKT worksheet.

questions.prompt: What distinguishes guided discovery from direct explanation?
options: Learners infer the rule through structured analysis
questions.correctAnswer: Learners infer the rule through structured analysis
questions.explanation: The teacher supports the process rather than immediately stating the rule.

questions.prompt: Which learner behaviour is central to guided discovery?
questions.correctAnswer: Noticing patterns in examples
questions.explanation: Learners analyse language evidence and derive generalisations.

questions.prompt: Which teacher action would undermine guided discovery?
options: State the rule before learners examine the examples
Ask focused questions about the examples
questions.correctAnswer: State the rule before learners examine the examples
questions.explanation: If the rule is supplied immediately, learners have little to discover.

questions.prompt: The teacher says “Stand up”, “Open the door”, and “Pick up the book”, and learners physically respond. Which approach is this?
questions.correctAnswer: Total Physical Response (TPR)
questions.explanation: TPR links language, especially instructions, with physical actions.

questions.prompt: Which sequence best represents Grammar-Translation?
options: Grammar rule → translation of a text
questions.correctAnswer: Grammar rule → translation of a text
questions.explanation: Grammar-Translation traditionally emphasises grammar explanation and translation.

questions.prompt: What is central in TPR?
questions.correctAnswer: Responding physically to language
questions.explanation: Learners demonstrate comprehension by carrying out actions.

questions.prompt: Which activity best fits Grammar-Translation?
options: Study a grammar rule and translate sentences between L1 and English
questions.correctAnswer: Study a grammar rule and translate sentences between L1 and English
questions.explanation: The approach foregrounds grammar knowledge and translation.

questions.prompt: Which statement most clearly contrasts TPR and Grammar-Translation?
options: TPR links meaning to physical action; Grammar-Translation focuses strongly on rules and translation
questions.correctAnswer: TPR links meaning to physical action; Grammar-Translation focuses strongly on rules and translation
questions.explanation: Their procedures and learning focus are fundamentally different.

questions.prompt: Learners listen to commands, perform the actions, then later give commands themselves. Which approach is this?
questions.correctAnswer: TPR
questions.explanation: Cambridge's TKT worksheet links TPR with instructions, learner actions and later learner instructions.

questions.prompt: Which lesson is most clearly Grammar-Translation?
options: The teacher explains a rule, then learners translate a passage
Learners solve a task before language focus
questions.correctAnswer: The teacher explains a rule, then learners translate a passage
questions.explanation: This is the classic Grammar-Translation sequence used in Cambridge's TKT materials.

questions.prompt: Which learner may find TPR particularly accessible at an early stage?
options: A learner who can show comprehension physically before producing much language
A learner who only wants literary translation
A learner doing advanced essay proofreading only
questions.correctAnswer: A learner who can show comprehension physically before producing much language
questions.explanation: TPR allows learners to demonstrate understanding through action.

questions.prompt: What is a limitation of using Grammar-Translation alone for communicative goals?
options: It may provide limited spontaneous interaction and spoken communication
It includes too much physical action
It always starts with a real-world task
questions.correctAnswer: It may provide limited spontaneous interaction and spoken communication
questions.explanation: Rule study and translation do not automatically provide extensive communicative use.

questions.prompt: Which pair is correctly matched?
options: TPR — instructions and physical actions; Grammar-Translation — rules and translation
TPR — lexical chunks; Grammar-Translation — free role-play
TPR — diagnostic task; Grammar-Translation — guided discovery
questions.correctAnswer: TPR — instructions and physical actions; Grammar-Translation — rules and translation
questions.explanation: These are the characteristic procedures of the two approaches.

questions.prompt: Learners notice and practise chunks such as “by the way” and “Would you mind...?” Which approach is this associated with?
questions.correctAnswer: Lexical Approach
questions.explanation: The Lexical Approach gives strong attention to words, collocations and multi-word chunks.

questions.prompt: Which sequence best represents a skills-based lesson?
options: Lead-in → key vocabulary → gist task → detail task → productive follow-up
questions.correctAnswer: Lead-in → key vocabulary → gist task → detail task → productive follow-up
questions.explanation: Cambridge's TKT worksheet uses this sequence for skills-based lessons.

questions.prompt: What does the Lexical Approach particularly encourage learners to notice?
questions.correctAnswer: Words, collocations and chunks
questions.explanation: Lexical teaching focuses on recurring combinations and chunks of language.

questions.prompt: In a reading lesson, learners first skim for gist, then read for detail, then discuss the topic. What framework is this?
questions.correctAnswer: Skills-based lesson
questions.explanation: The lesson is organised around staged development of receptive and productive skills.

questions.prompt: Which statement about a Lexical Approach is most accurate?
options: It treats recurring lexical chunks as important building blocks of language
It rejects vocabulary and focuses only on grammar rules
It always begins with a formal test
questions.correctAnswer: It treats recurring lexical chunks as important building blocks of language
questions.explanation: The approach highlights chunks, collocations and patterns of words in use.

questions.prompt: Learners underline useful phrases in a dialogue, discuss their meaning, then practise them. Which approach is this?
questions.correctAnswer: Lexical Approach
questions.explanation: The sequence of noticing chunks, discussing meaning and practising them matches Cambridge's Lexical Approach example.

questions.prompt: Which lesson sequence most strongly suggests a skills-based framework?
options: Lead-in → gist listening → detailed listening → speaking follow-up
questions.correctAnswer: Lead-in → gist listening → detailed listening → speaking follow-up
questions.explanation: Skills-based lessons often stage receptive work from general to detailed comprehension and then move to productive follow-up.

questions.prompt: What mainly distinguishes a skills-based lesson from PPP?
options: It is organised primarily around development of a language skill/subskills rather than presentation of one target language item
questions.correctAnswer: It is organised primarily around development of a language skill/subskills rather than presentation of one target language item
questions.explanation: A skills lesson is structured around reading, listening, speaking or writing processes and subskills.

questions.prompt: Which item would the Lexical Approach be especially likely to treat as a useful unit?
options: A frequent collocation such as “make a decision”
questions.correctAnswer: A frequent collocation such as “make a decision”
questions.explanation: Collocations and chunks are central lexical units in the approach.

questions.prompt: Which pair is correctly matched?
options: Lexical Approach — noticing chunks; Skills-based lesson — gist/detail/follow-up sequence
Lexical Approach — physical commands; Skills-based lesson — translation only
Lexical Approach — diagnostic test first; Skills-based lesson — no comprehension work
questions.correctAnswer: Lexical Approach — noticing chunks; Skills-based lesson — gist/detail/follow-up sequence
questions.explanation: These match the frameworks identified in Cambridge's TKT materials.
